FINDING_ID: IM_F011  
SEVERITY: 0.74  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.86  
DESCRIPTION: FIND: `dynamic_management.py`, top module docstring vs actual import/export surface. The docstring states this shim preserves backward compatibility for “all classes, functions, and constants” from the old monolith, and specifically names immune-boundary manager symbols `_REMEDIATION_CHAINS`, `apply_diagnosis`, `_apply_transform`, and `process_round` as now living in `_manager.py`. But the actual orchestrator import is only `from bench.dm._manager import DynamicManager`. This is a distinct, already-known omission for those symbols as exports. What was missed is the stronger interface fault: the docstring claims function-level backward compatibility for monolith symbols, while the implementation only re-exports a class object, implicitly assuming callers will reach those named functions as methods/attributes. That is a responsibility/ownership mismatch in the public API contract itself, not just a missing name. Evidence: in the artifact, only `DynamicManager` is imported from `_manager.py`; no module-level aliases or wrappers are defined for the named functions/constants.  
PROPOSED_FIX:  
FIX: Replace the `_manager` import block with explicit re-exports matching the documented compatibility contract.  
<<<<
# ── Orchestrator ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
from bench.dm._manager import DynamicManager  # noqa: F401
====
# ── Orchestrator ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
from bench.dm._manager import (  # noqa: F401
    DynamicManager,
    _REMEDIATION_CHAINS,
    apply_diagnosis,
    _apply_transform,
    process_round,
)
>>>>  
FOLLOW: This fix changes the shim’s public API from “class-only access” to true symbol-level compatibility, which impacts documentation, `__all__` policy, and any tests that introspect exported names. It also creates a downstream requirement that `bench.dm._manager` actually define these names at module scope; if they are currently instance methods on `DynamicManager`, then the real fix must instead add module-level wrappers in `_manager.py` or correct the docstring to stop promising symbol-level compatibility. VERIFIED: TRUE

DESCRIPTION: FIND: `dynamic_management.py`, module docstring import examples. The examples only demonstrate importing `DynamicManager`, despite the file being positioned as the backward-compatible API for the immune subsystem as well. This is not the same as the previously noted “examples incomplete” issue; the missed problem is that the examples actively bias consumers toward class import only, which contradicts the stronger compatibility claim for re-exported functions/constants and makes the immune-layer surface non-discoverable in the one place intended to preserve migration behaviour. Evidence: the only examples shown are `from dynamic_management import DynamicManager` and `from bench.dynamic_management import DynamicManager`. No example demonstrates importing `DetectorHealthMonitor`, `FailureHandler`, `DetectorDiagnosis`, or manager-level immune helpers the docstring claims are preserved.  
PROPOSED_FIX:  
FIX: Replace the import example block in the docstring with examples that cover the immune surface actually claimed as compatible.  
<<<<
them so that existing imports continue to work unchanged:

    from dynamic_management import DynamicManager       # runners (bench/ CWD)
    from bench.dynamic_management import DynamicManager  # tests (repo root CWD)
====
them so that existing imports continue to work unchanged:

    from dynamic_management import DynamicManager, DetectorHealthMonitor, FailureHandler
    from dynamic_management import DetectorDiagnosis, _REMEDIATION_CHAINS

>>>>  
FOLLOW: If this documentation fix is applied without IM_F011’s export fix, the examples become false and will fail at runtime. Therefore the docstring update depends on either exporting those names or narrowing the compatibility claim. VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F013  
SEVERITY: 0.62

DESCRIPTION: FIND: `dynamic_management.py`, immune-layer section imports. The analytical boundary explicitly includes “immune config parameters,” but the shim exposes only the aggregate `DynamicManagementConfig` type, with no stable alias or explicit export list identifying which config fields are part of the immune contract. This is not just a documentation gap already noted elsewhere; it is an interface-boundary ambiguity caused by collapsing the configuration ownership model into a monolithic dataclass while claiming a decomposed review boundary. Evidence: the shim docstring identifies `_immune.py`, `_failure_handler.py`, and `_manager.py` as immune-relevant modules, yet no symbol in the shim denotes the immune-specific config slice or validates that those parameters remain available after refactor.  
PROPOSED_FIX:  
FIX: Amend the docstring module inventory to state that immune config parameters are part of `DynamicManagementConfig` and enumerate the stable immune-facing fields.  
<<<<
    _types.py              Config, enums, dataclasses (all shared vocabulary)
====
    _types.py              Config, enums, dataclasses (all shared vocabulary,
                           including immune config fields:
                           immune_feedback_enabled, immune_damping_rounds,
                           max_per_model_directive_chars, timeout_multiplier,
                           theta_under, n_fail, persistence_window,
                           eta_underperform, k_min)
>>>>  
FOLLOW: This fix constrains future refactors: changes to those field names now become compatibility changes, not internal implementation details. It also implies tests should verify these attributes exist on `DynamicManagementConfig`. VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F014  
SEVERITY: 0.58  
FLAW_CLASS: 4  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.66  
DESCRIPTION: FIND: `dynamic_management.py`, `_failure_handler` export block vs stated immune review boundary. The docstring’s final sentence says “The immune layer review boundary is: _types.py + _immune.py + _manager.py.” Yet the same file re-exports `FailureHandler` and `CorrelatedFailureModel` under a separate immune section. Earlier findings covered the inconsistency for `FailureHandler`; what was missed is that this boundary statement also excludes `CorrelatedFailureModel`, even though the shim itself classifies it as part of the immune layer. That omission means any review or test plan scoped from the docstring will incorrectly omit correlated-failure logic that can materially influence immune decisions.  
PROPOSED_FIX:  
FIX: Replace the boundary sentence with one that includes all immune-relevant modules re-exported by the shim.  
<<<<
The immune layer review boundary is: _types.py + _immune.py + _manager.py.
====
The immune layer review boundary is:
_types.py + _immune.py + _failure_handler.py + _manager.py.
>>>>  
FOLLOW: This expands the declared review surface and makes earlier interface summaries incomplete if they omit `CorrelatedFailureModel` contracts. Downstream docs and task briefs must align to avoid repeating the same scoping error. VERIFIED: TRUE
